# FlutterGuard

> Manual Flutter APK and AAB security audits by Flutter engineer Mohamed Anas Fikhi (GWHYYY). Human review from the attacker's side: what is exposed, exploitable, and worth fixing — with evidence for every finding. No scanner-only noise.

- Canonical: https://flutterguard.dev/
- Contact: work@gwhyyy.com
- Booking: https://calendly.com/ffikhi-aanas/30min
- Reviewer: Mohamed Anas Fikhi — Flutter & Software Engineer, Casablanca / remote worldwide
- Profiles: https://github.com/anasfik — https://gwhyyy.com — https://linkedin.com/in/mohamed-anas-fikhi
- Source: https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard

## Scope

- APK/AAB anatomy, manifest attack surface, secrets and exposed configuration
- Flutter artifacts and libapp.so, network and backend boundary
- WebViews and platform bridges, signing and release posture, third-party SDK surface
- Context matters: a Firebase API key or missing certificate pinning is not automatically a vulnerability

## Method

1. Scope and authorize (APK/AAB you are authorized to share, test accounts where useful)
2. Reconstruct the attacker view (inspect, extract, fingerprint the release)
3. Verify, don't just flag (exploitability, prerequisites, impact)
4. Report and fix (prioritized findings, evidence, attack path, concrete fix, optional retest)

## Boundaries

- Active security testing only within explicitly authorized scope
- Third-party apps: lawful, non-invasive analysis of public artifacts only, unless written authorization exists
- Secrets and credentials minimized or redacted in reports

## FAQ (summary)

- Paid service is manual assessment, not an automated scan
- Minimum input: an APK or AAB you are authorized to have reviewed
- No invented certifications; findings can map to recognized mobile-security categories
- Retesting available after fixes

Full detail: https://flutterguard.dev/llms-full.txt
